name: Contract
description: The interfaces a project registers, and what source claims to implement them.

text: What this establishes is that a registered interface is implemented
somewhere in scope, and reached the way the specification says — never
that what it does behind that is right. It is the same sentence Behavior
turns on, and it licenses everything the mechanism cannot check.
Verification runs one way
An interface nothing claims is a difference, answered at the line
registering it, because that is where a reader chooses between writing
the code and dropping the contract. An interface nobody registered is
not one: only the contracts that matter are written down, so an absent
registration says nothing about the code.
A claim resolving to no contract belongs to the marker reading alone,
since it is about a claim and the syntax tree makes none. It is a
comparison that could not be made rather than a difference.
A name the other reading could resolve to no construct stops the
mechanism rather than answering. Read as Ruby, a route-shaped name is
undefined everywhere, and reporting that would blame the code for a
specification that lost its marker.
A second way in
A behavior may be claimed by as many tests as exercise it, but a
contract is the way in, so a second one is an entrance the specification
does not describe. Under the marker reading that is one interface
claimed in two places; under the other it is one name defined with two
shapes.
Which is why a method defined twice said nothing while only names were
compared: the name is the way in, and there was one of them. Definitions
agreeing on their shape are one way in still, so ordinary reopening goes
on saying nothing. Both places are answered, each naming the other,
since deciding which to keep means comparing them.
What is compared, and what stays out
A contract registering parameters is compared against them entire,
since a shape half-registered would let the rest drift; one registering
none asks for none to be compared, which is the same one-way rule.
Where the definitions disagree among themselves the contract is not also
compared against one of them: two entrances are already the answer.
The kind words a parameter carries are the language's own, and they
live in the reading that answers them. Contract compares them as text
without learning what any of them means, which is what lets a
specification stay silent about the language it is about — `include`
already says which files, and those files are read by whatever answers
for them.
`internal` is a fact about the interface rather than a preference about
pages, which is what separates it from a configuration switching a whole
specification off. A kind whose every interface is internal has nothing
to render at all.

scenarios.title: What the directory registers, and where
given: a contract directory holding several definitions
scenarios.then: each interface answers with its name, what it is for, and the line registering it

scenarios.title: A directory nobody wrote
given: a root with no contract directory
scenarios.then: no contracts are registered

scenarios.title: The words to look for
given: definitions naming their markers, two of them sharing one
scenarios.then: each word answers once, however many definitions claim it

scenarios.title: The same name under two markers
given: two definitions registering one name under different markers
scenarios.then: both are registered, because the marker is the namespace

scenarios.title: One name twice under one marker
given: two definitions registering the same name under the same marker
scenarios.then: the message names both places, relative to where the run started

scenarios.title: A contract with no name
given: a definition registering a contract that names nothing
scenarios.then: the file is named as registering a contract nothing can claim

scenarios.title: A definition with no marker
given: a definition that does not say what word claims it
scenarios.then: it is registered as one the syntax tree answers rather than refused

scenarios.title: A specification that will not parse
given: a contract definition that is not readable JSON
scenarios.then: the file is named as unreadable

scenarios.title: An interface nothing claims
given: a registered interface no claim in scope names
scenarios.then: it is answered at the line registering it, naming the scope that was searched

scenarios.title: A claim resolving to no contract
given: a claim naming something no definition registers under that marker
scenarios.then: the claim is answered at the line it sits on as resolving to no contract

scenarios.title: A claim naming no contract at all
given: a claim carrying its marker and nothing after it
scenarios.then: the claim is answered as naming no contract rather than being passed over

scenarios.title: One contract claimed in two places
given: two places claiming one registered interface
scenarios.then: each place is answered naming the other

scenarios.title: The document a definition becomes
given: a definition registering interfaces with descriptions
scenarios.then: the page carries the names and what each is for, and neither the marker nor the globs

scenarios.title: The files to look in
given: definitions whose includes cover different directories
scenarios.then: the union of every include answers, without repeats

scenarios.title: A contract no Ruby definition can be
given: a definition naming no marker
an interface named the way a route is named
scenarios.then: the file is named as registering something no Ruby definition can be

scenarios.title: An interface the syntax tree does not define
given: a definition naming no marker
names the source in scope declares, one of them missing
scenarios.then: the missing one is answered at the line registering it, naming the scope that was searched

scenarios.title: One name twice with no marker
given: two definitions naming no marker and registering the same name
scenarios.then: the message names both places without a namespace in front of the name

scenarios.title: An internal interface is verified like any other
given: a definition registering an internal interface nothing declares
scenarios.then: it is answered the way a published one would be

scenarios.title: The shape a contract registers
given: a contract registering parameters, one of them naming no kind
scenarios.then: the parameter naming no kind answers the one a bare name says

scenarios.title: An interface defined with another shape
given: a contract registering a shape
source defining that interface with another
scenarios.then: the interface answers at the line registering it, naming both shapes

scenarios.title: A contract registering no shape
given: a contract naming an interface and no parameters
source defining it with parameters
scenarios.then: nothing answers

scenarios.title: One name defined with two shapes
given: a registered interface defined twice, the two disagreeing on what a caller writes
scenarios.then: each definition answers, naming the other

scenarios.title: Definitions agreeing on their shape
given: a registered interface defined twice with the same parameters
scenarios.then: nothing answers

scenarios.title: Parameters registered under a marker
given: a contract file naming a marker and giving an interface parameters
scenarios.then: the file is named as one that cannot be read

scenarios.title: A name the specification uses at more than one depth
given: a contract file whose kind, one contract and one parameter of another are spelled alike
scenarios.then: each contract answers at the line declaring it

scenarios.title: The prose a specification carries for its document
given: a contract file writing notes under the kind and under one contract
scenarios.then: each note answers under the heading it hangs from

scenarios.title: A heading answers relative to where its notes hang
given: a note under a contract writing a heading at level 1
scenarios.then: the heading sits one level under the contract's own

scenarios.title: Notes under an interface the project does not publish
given: a contract marked internal writing notes of its own
scenarios.then: the document carries neither the interface nor its notes

scenarios.title: A note of a kind this document has no words for
given: a contract file writing a note whose type is none of the three
scenarios.then: the file is named as one that cannot be read

scenarios.title: A note whose text is not lines
given: a contract file writing a note whose text is one string
scenarios.then: the file is named as one that cannot be read

scenarios.title: A heading deeper than a page carries
given: a contract file writing a heading below the deepest level
scenarios.then: the file is named as one that cannot be read
